title: Steel alloying metals
h1: Niobium has one main source; for steel's other alloying metals, exposure depends on the buyer
deck: Brazil mined 93% of the world's niobium in 2024 and supplied most of every large importer's ferroniobium. Indonesia shipped 93% of traded ferronickel, almost all of it to China, and none of what the United States imported.

chokepoint.physics: Two companies in Brazil and one in Canada produce nearly all niobium. Most of it goes into steel, at a few hundred grams per tonne
chokepoint.share: 93% of niobium mined (2024); Brazil supplied 54% to 98% of ferroniobium imports in six large markets

niobium.usgs_text: Brazil continued to be the world's leading niobium producer, accounting for approximately 93% of global production, followed by Canada with 5%.
niobium.brazil_exports_text: Most of Brazil's exports went to China (49%), followed by the Netherlands (17%), Singapore (9%), and the Republic of Korea and the United States (8% each).
niobium.us_end_use: Major end-use distribution of domestic niobium consumption was estimated as follows: steels, about 77%, and superalloys, about 23%.
niobium.world_steel_share_2022: Steel, primarily HSLA steel used in structural, automotive, and aerospace applications, accounted for approximately 89% of global niobium consumption
niobium.producers: Two companies produce these materials in Brazil, and one company produces them in Canada.
niobium.producers_named: In Brazil, the leading producers of niobium were Companhia Brasileira de Metalurgia e Mineracao (CBMM) and Niobras Mineracao Ltda. [a subsidiary of China Molybdenum Co., Ltd. (China)]. In Canada, the leading producer was Niobec Inc.
niobium.cbmm_capacity_quote: we maintain a production capacity (150,000 tonnes/ year) that exceeds global consumption

yearbook_2022_t_niobium.note: Minerals Yearbook 2022, table 4, mineral concentrates, niobium content; the Brazilian figure is an estimate.

niobium.third_brazilian_producer_note: Mineracao Taboca, niobium and tantalum ferroalloys, gross weight, 2022, as reported by USGS.
niobium.us_ferroniobium_sources: Ferroniobium and niobium metal: Brazil, 65%; Canada, 31%; and other, 4%.
niobium.recycling: it may have been as much as 20% of apparent consumption

chromium.ferrochrome_text: China was the leading producer of ferrochromium, with an estimated 49% of global production (table 8).
chromium.chromite_text_2023: South Africa was the leading producer of chromite ore, with an estimated 44% of global production.

oecd_2024.note: Figure 2 of the OECD report, which gives the International Chromium Development Association as its source. Read from the chart labels on page 15.
oecd_2024.ferrochrome_text: In 2024, the total world production of ferrochrome was estimated at around 18.5 million tonnes, a 15% increase from 2023
oecd_2024.china_text: more than half of ferrochromium was produced in China
oecd_2024.ore_text_usgs: accounting for an estimated 45% of total world mining production

chromium.oecd_use: Around 90% to 95% of mined chrome ore is converted into ferrochrome, and the stainless-steel sector accounts for 80% to 90% of global ferrochrome use
chromium.oecd_exports: These two countries together account for about 88% of global chromium ore exports.
chromium.oecd_restrictions: chromium ore exports from both South Africa and Zimbabwe are affected by some form of export restrictions
chromium.usgs_potential: Potential export controls and tariffs on chromite ore from South Africa may also affect ferrochromium production in China.
chromium.usgs_substitute: Chromium has no substitute in stainless steel, the leading end use, or in superalloys, the major strategic end use.
chromium.usgs_recycling: recycled chromium (contained in reported stainless-steel scrap receipts) accounted for 21% of apparent consumption
chromium.stainless_minimum: Stainless steels are corrosion resistant steels with a minimum of 10.5 per cent of chromium (Cr).

vanadium.usgs_coproduct: In 2025, China continued to be the world's top vanadium producer, with most of its production originating as a coproduct from vanadiferous titanomagnetite ores processed during steelmaking.
vanadium.usgs_byproduct_note: Because vanadium is typically recovered as a byproduct or coproduct, demonstrated world resources of the element are not fully indicative of available supplies.
vanadium.vanitec_text: Coproduct steelmaking slag resulting from the processing of titaniferous magnetite ore supports about 59% of global vanadium.
vanadium.us_use: Metallurgical use, primarily as an alloying agent for iron and steel, accounted for more than 90% of domestic reported vanadium consumption in 2025.
vanadium.substitution: Replacement of vanadium with other mineral commodities requires significant technical adjustments to the steel production process to ensure that product specifications and quality are not compromised.
vanadium.substitution_time: substitution for vanadium is normally not considered for short-term changes in market conditions because of the considerable effort involved in implementing the change
vanadium.usgs_interchangeable: Certain metals, such as manganese, molybdenum, niobium (columbium), titanium, and tungsten, are to some degree interchangeable with vanadium as alloying elements in steel.

nickel.us_use: Stainless and alloy steel and nickel-containing alloys typically account for more than 85% of domestic consumption.
nickel.us_recycling: nickel recovered from scrap accounted for approximately 60% of apparent consumption
nickel.oecd_refined: Indonesia's share of global refined nickel output rose from 6% in 2015 to 61% in 2024
nickel.oecd_ban: since 2020, Indonesia has imposed a full ban on nickel ore exports

other_metals.manganese_substitute: Manganese has no satisfactory substitute in its major applications.
other_metals.molybdenum_substitute: There is little substitution for molybdenum in its major application in steels and cast irons.
other_metals.niobium_substitute: molybdenum and vanadium as alloying elements in high-strength low-alloy steels
other_metals.niobium_substitute_caveat: a performance loss or higher cost may ensue
other_metals.molybdenum_recycling: may be as much as 30% of the apparent supply of molybdenum

grades.note: Composition limits in per cent by weight, from producer data sheets that name the covering standard, and from the standard's own page for A572.
grades.a572_scope: The use of columbium (niobium), vanadium, titanium, nitrogen, or combinations thereof, within the limitations noted in Section 5, is required; the selection of type (1, 2, 3, or 5) is at the option of the producer, unless otherwise specified by the purchaser.
grades.grades_count: There are more than 3,500 different grades of steel with many different physical, chemical, and environmental properties.

trade_boundaries.720293: Ferro-niobium. The alloy in which most niobium is traded; about 65% niobium by weight.
trade_boundaries.720292: Ferro-vanadium. Sold in grades from about 40% to 80% vanadium, so tonnage is not vanadium content.
trade_boundaries.720241: Ferro-chromium with more than 4% carbon. The grade used for most stainless steel.
trade_boundaries.720211: Ferro-manganese with more than 2% carbon. Ferro-silico-manganese is a separate code.

content_inputs.note: Metal content of traded ferroalloys by origin. For most alloys the content is measured: US customs records both gross weight and contained metal for each tariff line and country, and the figure here is contained weight divided by gross weight for US imports from that origin, in 2024 where the flow was at least the threshold tonnage and otherwise in the latest such year from 2022 to 2025. It is a measurement of what the United States imported, applied here to what that origin shipped to everyone. Origins with no flow above the threshold in any of the four years take the range of the measured origins for that code, except where a note says otherwise.

Indonesia.basis: USGS production estimates for Indonesia, 2024: nickel pig iron 11,000,000 t gross with 1,600,000 t of nickel, and ferronickel 101,000 t gross with 20,103 t of nickel. Both nickel pig iron figures are USGS estimates. The low end, 12.2%, is the nickel grade one producer reports for its own nickel pig iron in 2024. Not measured on trade: the United States imports none.

720292.other_origins_basis: USGS Minerals Yearbook 2023, Vanadium: "FeV was available as alloys containing either 45%-to-50% or 80% vanadium."

720293.other_origins_basis: USGS: "Contained weight calculated assuming 65% contained Nb" (Minerals Yearbook 2022, Ferroalloys, table 7, footnote 2). An assumption, not a measurement; US customs records no content for ferroniobium. USGS Professional Paper 1802-M gives the range: ferroniobium "contains 60 to 70 percent niobium".
